messages.noArrowFunctionsInWatch: You should not use an arrow function to define a watcher.

cases.code:
<script lang="ts">
        export default {
          watch: {
            foo: function() {}
          },
        }
      </script>

<script lang="ts">
        export default {
          watch: {
            foo() {},
            bar() {}
          },
        }
      </script>

<script lang="ts">
        export default {
          watch: {
            foo: function() {},
            bar: function() {}
          },
        }
      </script>

<script lang="ts">
        export default {
          watch: {
            ...obj,
            foo: function() {},
            bar: function() {}
          },
        }
      </script>

<script lang="ts">
      export default {
        data: {
          a: 1,
          b: 2,
          c: 3,
          d: 4,
          e: {
            f: {
              g: 5
            }
          }
        },
        watch: {
          a: function (val, oldVal) {
            console.log('new: %s, old: %s', val, oldVal)
          },
          b: 'someMethod',
          c: {
            handler: function (val, oldVal) {},
            deep: true
          },
          d: {
            handler: 'someMethod',
            immediate: true
          },
          e: [
            'handle1',
            function handle2 (val, oldVal) {},
            {
              handler: function handle3 (val, oldVal) {},
              /* ... */
            }
          ],
          'e.f': function (val, oldVal) { /* ... */ }
        }
      }</script>
